mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative mean return over triggered 60-day horizons at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million annualized units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative mean return over triggered 60-day horizons at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5 percentage points month-over-month for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressure and prompts preemptive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months indicates broad-based demand weakness, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12-month MA AND RSAFS < 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.
